historia.title: Historia del Tribunal Supremo Electoral

classes.name: Elección de Presidente y Vicepresidente de la República
classes.note: President and Vice President elected together on one ticket (planilla) by absolute majority of valid votes, else a second election between the two leading tickets 45 to 60 days later (Constitution art. 184; LEPP art. 201). classes.name: Diputados al Congreso de la República por lista nacional
classes.note: The Congreso de la República is unicameral. Deputies are elected by closed lists and D'Hondt, part by electoral district (each department, with Guatemala City's municipality as the Distrito Central and the rest of its department as the Distrito de Guatemala) and part by a national list equal to a quarter of the district seats (Constitution art. 157; LEPP arts. 203 and 205). Seats per district follow population (one per 80,000 inhabitants in 2007), capped at 128 district seats since 2016. In 1985 the national list was voted with the presidential ticket; from 1990 on a separate ballot. The extraordinary election of 14 August 1994, after the consulta of 30 January 1994, renewed the whole Congress for the rest of the term.

cadence.vacancy_rule: The next candidate on the party's list takes the seat (LEPP art. 204).

classes.name: Consulta popular
classes.note: Called by Congress on decisions of special importance (Constitution art. 173) and required to ratify constitutional reforms that Congress passes by two thirds (art. 280); the 2018 consulta on the dispute with Belize was held under transitory art. 19. Three held: 30 January 1994 (the 1993 reforms, approved), 16 May 1999 (the reforms after the peace accords, four questions, all rejected), and 15 April 2018 (the Belize dispute to the International Court of Justice, approved). Two requests in 1993, after the self-coup of 25 May, were withdrawn or rejected before a vote.

classes.name: Diputados a la Asamblea Nacional Constituyente
classes.note: Elected on 1 July 1984, 88 deputies, 23 by national list and 65 by district, the TSE's first election; it wrote the 1985 Constitution and the LEPP. The Constitution lets Congress call a new one by two thirds to amend its protected articles (art. 278; LEPP art. 199 b). The assemblies that wrote the 1945, 1956, and 1965 constitutions were elected before the TSE existed and fall under legislativa_previa.

classes.name: Elección de Alcaldes y Corporaciones Municipales
classes.finest_note: One list per organization; the leading list takes the mayoralty and the síndicos by plurality, councillors by D'Hondt
classes.note: Each of the 340 municipalities elects its concejo: the mayor and síndicos by plurality of the list and the councillors by D'Hondt, with 2 or 3 síndicos and 4 to 10 councillors by population (Constitution art. 254; LEPP arts. 202, 203, and 206). Civic electoral committees (comités cívicos) may stand alongside parties. Until the 1993 reforms terms were two and a half or five years by size, so mid-term elections fell in 1988, 1993, and 1998 (corporacion_medio_periodo); since 1999 every municipality votes with the general election for four years. Where null votes exceed half, the election is repeated (LEPP art. 203 bis), as in five municipalities on 20 August 2023.

classes.note: Presidents were chosen by direct vote under the constitutions of 1879, 1945, 1956, and 1965, and under the last two by Congress between the two leading candidates when none had an absolute majority. The coup of 23 March 1982 ended the 1965 order and annulled that month's election.

classes.disposition_reason: Before the Tribunal Supremo Electoral (Decreto Ley 30-83), elections were run by the Registro Electoral and earlier bodies under the Executive; the TSE's memorias begin with 1984 and no official compilation of earlier results is published.

classes.name: Asambleas de partidos políticos y comités cívicos
classes.note: Each party's Asamblea Nacional elects and proclaims its candidates for President, Vice President, the national list, and the Central American Parliament, and departmental and municipal assemblies those for districts and corporations (LEPP arts. 24-27); a TSE delegate attends and the acta is filed with the Registro de Ciudadanos.
classes.locator: https://www.tse.org.gt/images/LEPP2026.pdf (art. 26 e: "Elegir y proclamar a los candidatos del partido, a la Presidencia")
classes.disposition_reason: Votes of party delegates in assemblies, not a primary open to voters; the TSE certifies the actas but runs no nominating election and publishes no counts.

classes.name: Elección de magistrados y funcionarios por el Congreso
classes.name_en: Judges and officers chosen by Congress
classes.note: Congress elects the Supreme Court and Court of Appeals magistrates from postulation-commission lists (Constitution arts. 215 and 217), the five TSE magistrates from a list of 40 (LEPP art. 123), and the Comptroller and Human Rights Ombudsman; the Constitutional Court's members are designated by the Supreme Court, Congress, the President, the University of San Carlos, and the bar association (art. 269).
classes.locator: https://www.tse.org.gt/images/LEPP2026.pdf (art. 123: elected by Congress "de una nómina de cuarenta candidatos propuesta por la Comisión de Postulación")
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by Congress or by institutions, with no popular vote.

classes.name: Elecciones de colegios profesionales y de la Universidad de San Carlos
classes.name_en: Professional-association and university elections for public posts
classes.note: Members of the colegios profesionales elect delegates to the postulation commissions and the bar association's magistrates of the Constitutional Court (Constitution art. 269); the University of San Carlos's council designates another.
classes.disposition_reason: Run by each colegio's own electoral tribunal for its members, not by the TSE, and not general elections.

classes.name: Consultas a los vecinos
classes.note: A municipal council may consult its residents, and must when 10 percent of them ask; communities have also held consultations under ILO Convention 169, notably on mining since 2005 (Código Municipal, Decreto 12-2002, arts. 63-66).
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the municipality, not the TSE; results stay in each council's actas and no register of them is published.

classes.name: Alcaldías comunitarias o auxiliares
classes.note: Each community's assembly chooses its alcalde comunitario or auxiliar by its own customs, and the municipal mayor appoints the one chosen (Código Municipal, Decreto 12-2002, arts. 56-58).
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by community assemblies by custom, not by ballot under the LEPP; no electoral authority runs or records them.

classes.name: Consejos Comunitarios de Desarrollo (COCODE)
classes.note: Each community's general assembly elects its COCODE's coordinating body (Ley de los Consejos de Desarrollo Urbano y Rural, Decreto 11-2002, art. 13).
classes.disposition_reason: Elected by show of hands in community assemblies, not by ballot under the LEPP; no electoral authority runs or records them.
